threads.body:
This group is also used by `gen_ai.invoke_agent.internal`, which covers `invoke_workflow` (LangGraph, CrewAI `Crew`) and `invoke_{framework_entrypoint}` (e.g. `invoke_runner`), where there may be no single agent — and with OpenAI Agents `Runner.run` handoffs, the active agent changes mid-run. Maybe something like "The tools available to the invoked agent, workflow, or entrypoint for this invocation", plus guidance on multi-agent cases (union vs. omit)?

Also, "associated with" is ambiguous for tools that change at runtime (MCP discovery, `is_enabled` callbacks, per-step filtering) — configured vs. effective set?

threads.body: The explicit `tools=[]` overrides passed by `_on_committed` and `_finish_tool_call_generation` never reach telemetry because this truthiness check drops them. Those generations omit `gen_ai.tool.definitions` instead of recording `[]`, so consumers cannot distinguish a known empty tool set from unavailable or uncaptured definitions. Record the resolved list even when it is empty so the reference demonstrates both session inheritance and the empty override.

threads.body:
This guidance is only about `gen_ai.tool.definitions`, so it would fit better as a note on the attribute ref below than in the span note. Something like:

```yaml
      - ref: gen_ai.tool.definitions
        requirement_level: opt_in
        brief: The list of tool definitions supplied to the model for this inference operation.
        note: |
          > [!WARNING]
          > This attribute may contain sensitive information.

          For providers with session-level tools and per-generation overrides, record
          the generation's tools if set, otherwise the session's tools.

          Since this attribute could be large, it's NOT RECOMMENDED to populate
          non-required properties by default. Instrumentations MAY provide a way
          to enable populating optional properties.
```
